correctness.rationale: Deleting a point turns missing surviving t-subsets into S(t−1,t,v−1), so any fixed t-anchor has one old-block completion plus t distinct missing-replacement points and exactly v−2t−2 free points if covered, while an uncovered anchor forces one missing tuple with all outside choices. These local types are exactly what a reusable (t+1)-pebble strategy must maintain and are independent of rounds; repeated pebbles handled by equality. The full-vs-puncture sentence detects uncovered t-tuples; P0-vs-P+ uses a covered t-anchor and one free outside witness with variable reuse within separate Cov subformulas. FO^t atoms are always false due to arity. Independent SQS(8,10) extension-pattern checks covered 1,120 anchor cases; finite checks are only corroboration.
